podcast.title: Breakup (2008)
podcast.body: The Dresden Dolls disbanded in 2008 after failing to achieve a mainstream breakthrough, despite their excellence. "a mainstream breakthrough eluded them and they broke up in 2008."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Boston Origin and Cabaret Sound
podcast.body: This two-piece group from Boston has a unique sound and look, described as if Siouxsie and the Banshees were performing in East Berlin cabarets in 1932. "There are two piece groups out of Boston and they look and sound like what might have happened had Suzy and the Banshee's been playing the Cabaret's and East Berlin in 1932."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Goth Enough for Tours
podcast.body: The Dresden Dolls' "kind of sort of Goth" style was sufficiently Goth-aligned to earn them an invitation to tour with Nine Inch Nails, demonstrating their acceptance within the broader alternative scene. "Goth enough to be invited on tour with Nine-Hitch Nails"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Two-Piece, Highly Visual Outfit
podcast.body: The Dresden Dolls was a two-piece band known for its highly visual presentation, with Amanda Palmer joining when she was about 27. "Her first real band was The Dresden Dolls, a two-piece outfit that was highly visual."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Solo Career (Post-2008)
xref.body: After The Dresden Dolls disbanded in 2008, Amanda Palmer pursued a solo career, performing numerous gigs, theater productions, writing books, and releasing an album of Radiohead songs played on ukulele, developing a strong cult following. "From there she went solo, lots of gigs, lots of theater, lots of critical acclaim, a couple of books."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
